texts.preamble: Ram Bahadur vs State Of U.P. on 18 January, 2020 Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Court No. - 13 Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 103 of 2014
texts.facts: 4. The revisionist is a milkman, whose milk was taken for testing on 22nd May, 2006 by the Food Inspector. The Public Analyst, in his report dated 26th June, 2006, opined that the milk fat was was 5.3% and milk solids-not-fat was 7.1% and, thus, it was opined that the milk solids-not-fat was 16% less than the prescribed limit. The Central Food Laboratory also examined the sample, which was sent to it on request of the revisionist. The report of the Central Food Laboratory dated 2nd March, 2010 has been placed on record. According to the said report, the milk fat was 6%, and it was above the prescribed limit of 4.5%, however, the milk solids-not-fat was found to be 6.1%, which is less than 8.5%. 5. Counsel for the revisionist submits that the milk fat was not injurious to human health; only the milk solids-not-fat was less than the prescribed limit inasmuch as in the report of Public Analyst it was found 7.1%, and it was less than the standard limit of 8.5%.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel further submits that the incident took place around 14 years before; the revisionist has undergone around 35 days imprisonment. The learned counsel places reliance on judgment in 'Sughar Singh Vs. State and another' (Criminal Revision No.985 of 1991) in which this Court, after considering the facts of the case, which are identical to the present one, found the offence to be of very minor nature. The milk solids-not-fat was not injurious to the health. 6. The Supreme Court in Nand Lal v. State of Uttarakhand and others, 2010 (4) SCC 562, after considering the age of the appellant in that case, and taking into account the fact that the incident was very old, reduced the sentence to the period already undergone.

The learned counsel places reliance on judgment in 'Sughar Singh Vs.
